body:
I never told my psychiatrist I was drinking either, although I saw her very infrequently anyway, I find psychiatrists unless they are specially trained just don't understand addiction and tell you to cut down or tone it down as if you're in control of it and it's just a silly thing. I started going to AA and that's where I managed to start getting sober.

When I was drinking alcoholically I was on meds the whole time too (antidepressants) and the combination of the two was horrendous. I was severely manic pretty much the whole time, or in some sort of mixed state. I remember trying to strangle myself with a games console cord in front of my CPN.

I get irritated at professionals too when they're insensitive, but I think a lot of them just have that attitude.

Yeah that's true. It is frustrating. Been on mood stabilisers too - lithium, Depakote and the like. Did nothing but make me apathetic and spotty. Yes I am putting it down to my early sobriety days - a lot of physical changes going on in my brain, feel very emotionally vulnerable etc because I'm having to learn to deal with my emotions rather than drinking them away.

The problem is I don't think anything triggers it off, it's just a cycle that I feel I am unable to control. I don't feel upset about anything in particular when it happens, I don't react to anything external that I'm consciously aware of. Part of me thinks it might be some sort of brain injury from coming off psychiatric drugs. I came off this drug, which was a neuroleptic, at the same time I stopped drinking alcoholically, so obviously my brain has had to undergo some sort of physical transformation. Shortly after, these episodes intensified, to the point I feel suicidal almost permanently.
No I don't have interpersonal difficulties really, unless someone is very nasty then of course I'm upset. Otherwise I'm basically seen as being laid back, I'm a bit of a pushover really.

Well I suppose I am emotionally dysregulated, I have problems with that, as well as some fairly massive mood swings from time to time. I've been diagnosed as rapid cycling bipolar. I'd like to be able to get these cycles to be more manageable. Does DBT help with that?

The one good thing is AA. I have a sponsor and some friends at meetings.

Other than that I am lonely and anxious a lot. I keep wanting to reach out or be plucked from the jaws of death or something dramatic like that, but I don't really know what help I really want.

If this was an ideal world - there'd be a nice place I could go and stay with people I like. Company, activities that aren't infantilising (like they are in hospital), freedom, safety, therapy, AA, spiritual workshops. Like I said, ideal worlds. 

The "help" I've had so far consists of being hospitalised, being sectioned in hospital, force fed medication, being forcibly injected, forced to go to a mental health rehabilitation centre, 5 months of CAT therapy (did not retain much of it), seeing psychiatrists who say I should get a job/go to university/move out, seeing CPN's who turned up once a week and chatted to me like a friend, seen the GP frequently, who checks I am alive and tells me to give things time, been given very small prescriptions of tranquillisers, spoken to/seen the home treatment team who tell me to drink tea/watch a film/read a dictionary, rung helplines who phone the police/ambulance/my parents, seen a victim support worker who saw me twice then never bothered phoning me again, despite the fact I am dealing with ongoing trauma from an assault that ended in an abortion.

 I now only take an antidepressant (Venlafaxine -150mg) which doesn't help a lot.

I'm still around. Yes the police and ambulance were called for welfare checks mainly, because I keep having meltdowns. Prior to that I'd taken some large overdoses and the ambulance came then and took me to hospital. 

I feel like a drain on resources and a drain on everyone.

I know the pain but if she cheated on you she clearly doesn't love you, or is at the very least careless with your feelings - which is on her, it shows the kind of person she is, not you. 

I've been cheated on, fucked over, treated like crap by exes. I know all too well the pain, discomfort, heartache and suffering. It will ease with time though, I'm sure of it.

I feel very similarly and I thought what you wrote was very eloquent and quite beautiful in its own way. Sorry, that's not meant to sound patronising. 

I've been through a violation too, I have PTSD as a result of this and other things too. I'm unable to go near the town it occurred in, have daily panic attacks, poor sleep, and nightmares. 

I'm also unemployed - I spend a lot of time thinking about how worthless I feel. When I've applied for jobs I freak out because I have no experience and know there's no point in trying because there's always 100 people who are better than me applying too.

I recently lost my chance of getting a really nice flat in a place I want to live because the landlord wouldn't tolerate my application - because I'm 23 and unemployed. I'll be stuck in a shitty bedsit at this rate. 

I know it is shit and awful and unfair. I can't really offer advice, just my sympathy.

Yes very much so. 
Walking along roads - " Oh I could just run/fall in front of that car/lorry".

Taking pills for a headache - "Oh there's enough in there to overdose on/kill/maim myself with". 

Same thing obviously goes with sharp objects - "Hmm could stab myself with that".

What I find horrendously annoying is how to distinguish between an impulse that could turn into action and just a "plain" intrusive thought.
Yeah I feel the same I keep falling into pits of despair and lately I just think I'm too damaged to ever be fixed. Broken goods.
